source_observations: Figures 2 and 6b label the middle-southern corridor Gifford River.
Figure 2 labels Bell Bay and Saputing Lake and depicts local drainage toward the southern Bell Bay shoreline.
The green glacial-lake polygons and cold/warm-based zones describe former glacial conditions; they do not establish present ice cover, modern water levels or active ice-to-river transitions.
The southern selected transfer between the Gifford and Saputing Lake-side corridors is not continuously established.

Figure 6 background geology is modified from de Kemp and Scott1998 and Lebeau et al.2020; panel b shows samples from this study. No separately cited older map was reopened. No wholly independent underlying hydrographic datasets are claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen upper Silver Creek opening and mountain-valley corridor
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is in the mapped Silver Creek valley near Meadow Valley, downstream of the mapped headward Silver Creek reaches. The selected southwestward turn and subsequent southward canyon are supported by repeated Silver Creek labels and connected channel cartography. Allison Creek, Stone Corral Creek, Copper Creek and other labeled tributary junctions are visible in the upper corridor. Delintment Lake is an adjacent tributary-basin feature, not a selected through-lake passage. The opening is not asserted to be the natural or formally registered source of Silver Creek.

correspondence.component_scope: Silver Creek canyon, lower mountain junctions and broad valley
correspondence.finding: The overlapping upper and middle views show the continuous named Silver Creek canyon into the broad wet valley and its southeastward bend toward Riley. The mapped Sawmill Creek, Wickiup Creek and Nicoll Creek junction settings are distinguishable from the selected Silver Creek course. The many short stored joins here stay in this mapped river corridor; none requires inventing an additional tributary name.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected southwestward transfer near Riley and Chickahominy Creek
correspondence.finding: The original maps distinguish Silver Creek along the northern/eastern valley and Chickahominy Creek approaching Riley from the west, with their downstream common Silver Creek corridor. The chosen line moves southwest across the intervening field/drainage-grid setting, reaches the Chickahominy Creek side near the highway, then turns east and southeast. The source does not clearly establish that chosen inter-channel through-transfer. The confluence setting and both names are supported, but nearby channels and a shared receiving stream are insufficient to close the selected passage. Chickahominy Reservoir lies on the western tributary and is not traversed by this selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Silver Creek below Riley, Moon Reservoir and downstream outlet canyon
correspondence.finding: The named Silver Creek corridor south of Riley enters the waterbody labeled Moon Reservoir, traverses its long north-south impounded valley, and continues through the mapped outlet canyon toward the lower wetland. Both reservoir approach and continuation are readable. The source supports this bounded river-reservoir-river geographic correspondence without a claim about current reservoir level, dam operation, exact banks or instantaneous flow.

correspondence.component_scope: Cote Slough and lower Silver Creek wetland/canal passage to Harney Lake
correspondence.finding: The maps show Cote Slough and repeated Silver Creek labels, nearby Stinking Lake and Derrick Lake, and the Saint Clair and Goulden canal setting near Double O Ranch Road. Silver Creek is visibly represented in the lower wetland and at the western Harney Lake margin. The selected long southward and southeastward line also crosses intervening marsh and managed-channel terrain west of portions of the labeled creek. These originals do not establish the complete chosen through-passage among those wetland and canal sections. The nearby lakes and canal labels are retained as context, not automatically substituted as the selected route.

correspondence.component_scope: Harney Lake crossing and eastern intermittent link toward Mud Lake
correspondence.finding: The selected long eastward passage is in the mapped Harney Lake basin. At its eastern side an unnamed dashed blue connection is actually depicted across the narrow separation into the southern Mud Lake wetland/lake setting. This supplies ordinary cartographic correspondence for that inter-lake crossing; it is not treated as a missing link merely because the two lakes have separate names. Harney Lake and the nearby Hughet Creek label are distinct feature contexts, not proof that the whole lake crossing is a reach named Silver Creek. No current direction, seasonality measurement or continuous present-day flow is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastward passage within Mud Lake
correspondence.finding: The following northeastward parts traverse the original mapped Mud Lake and wetland extent. The interior lake/wetland setting and approach toward its northeastern side are readable. Mud Lake is a supported component name, not a representative river name for the selected system.

correspondence.component_scope: Mud Lake to western Malheur Lake through the highway/Narrows wetland
correspondence.finding: The original shows the northeastern Mud Lake margin, Frenchglen Highway and the adjacent western Malheur Lake marsh and shore country. The selected line crosses this narrowed wetland/road belt and continues along the western lake-margin setting. Geographic surroundings are readable, but a continuous selected through-passage across the road/wetland interval is not established by the inspected cartography. Shared wetland shading and adjacent lake labels alone do not supply that missing linkage. This is a source-correspondence gap, not a finding that the lakes never connect.

correspondence.component_scope: Final eastward part and actual endpoint inside Malheur Lake
correspondence.finding: The last eastward part ends within the water area labeled Malheur Lake, away from the lower Silver Creek mouth at Harney Lake. The actual modeled endpoint is therefore directly accounted for as an interior Malheur Lake setting. West Fork and East Fork Silvies River and Donner und Blitzen River are neighboring inflow context, not names assigned to this selected line. No ocean outlet or natural river mouth is claimed at the endpoint.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern unlabelled opening and first westward links
correspondence.finding: The retained original Figure 6b depicts the thin westward drainage and its turn toward the southwestern feeder at the selected eastern opening. Figure 2 places this interval in a reconstructed glacial-lake setting, but that green thematic polygon is not evidence of a present lake or active ice passage. The opening has no separately established hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern feeder, lake-arm passage and intervening joins
correspondence.finding: The west-to-southwestern feeder reaches the western side of the elongated, unlabelled waterbody shown in white in Figure 6b, then continues southwest along its short western arm and connected drainage. The selected corridor and intervening joins can be followed at generalized map scale. The whole eastward extent of that waterbody is not selected, and no lake name or uniform river name is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle southwestern and westward Gifford River corridor
correspondence.finding: Figures 2 and 6b show the southwestern continuation in the labelled Gifford River corridor. This supports Gifford River as a bounded component candidate. The label and mapped middle drainage do not establish the later selected westward transfer to the Saputing Lake side.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected southern westward transfer and turn toward the Saputing Lake side
correspondence.finding: The selection continues west across the southern lowland toward the Saputing Lake side and then bends northwest. Both inspected panels show local streams and small waterbodies here, but a continuous selected connection from the Gifford corridor across this interval is not clearly established. The river labels and shared lowland setting do not supply the missing through-link. This is an actual geographic correspondence gap, not a completed naming-scope hold.

correspondence.component_scope: Saputing Lake-side northern outlet and southern Bell Bay terminal
correspondence.finding: Figure 2 depicts the short northward drainage reaching the southern end of Bell Bay beside the Saputing Lake setting, and Figure 6b independently exposes the same local drainage beneath the thematic overprint. The selected final reach and actual terminal setting correspond at regional scale. The source does not justify assigning the Saputing lake name or Gifford River name uniformly to this outlet, nor does this local match resolve the preceding southern transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen small headward feeder and entry into the Braço do Norte corridor
correspondence.finding: The northern Anitápolis sheet depicts the chosen eastward then southeastward small feeder and its entry into the north–south river corridor east of the Anitápolis seat. Adjacent feeder labels are not assigned to the selected opening. The opening and join are geographically accounted for at ordinary map scale; its own hydronym is unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Rio Braço do Norte and Anitápolis-area tributary convergence
correspondence.finding: Both Anitápolis sheets show the connected southward course repeatedly labeled Rio Braço do Norte, the tributary convergence east/south of the municipal seat and continuation toward Santa Rosa de Lima. Their overlapping map areas account for the stored joins across the sheet split. The selected route is distinguished from the separate river through the Anitápolis seat.

correspondence.component_scope: Santa Rosa de Lima, Rio Fortuna, Braço do Norte and São Ludgero corridor
correspondence.finding: The state original shows the continuous southward river corridor from the Anitápolis map coverage through Santa Rosa de Lima and Rio Fortuna to Braço do Norte and São Ludgero. The selected short parts and joins occupy this same connected valley at regional scale. Generalized linework supports corridor identity, without assigning every feeder label or exact confluence vertex.

correspondence.component_scope: Braço do Norte–Tubarão convergence and Tubarão urban continuation
correspondence.finding: The state original depicts the Braço do Norte corridor joining the eastward lower trunk and its continuation through the Tubarão urban setting toward Capivari de Baixo. Chapter II prose independently identifies Braço do Norte as a Tubarão tributary. This supplies ordinary convergence and trunk correspondence through the end of the first fragment; the name-change point is not assigned to a particular stored vertex.

correspondence.component_scope: Continuation across the fragment boundary and lower Tubarão approach
correspondence.finding: The overlapping state and Laguna map coverage places the second fragment on the connected lower river approach from Tubarão. Its beginning continues the first fragment at the same corridor. The regional original shows a trunk flowing toward the lagoon complex, while the finer municipal map supplies the western approach to the lowland network.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected eastward lowland traverse and turn toward the southern lagoons
correspondence.finding: The Laguna original depicts multiple fine drainage lines, wetland lowlands, roads and different routes toward the lagoon complex. It does not establish a continuous watercourse matching the complete selected long eastward traverse and its southeastern turn. A nearby river, road, basin label or modeled join cannot supply that missing through-link. Whether any selected part represents an engineered connection is unresolved.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern lagoon entrance, intervening narrow waters and southern continuation
correspondence.finding: The Laguna original shows the eastern lagoon, branching narrow water areas and their southern connection into the lagoon labeled Lagoa de Garopaba do Sul on the acquired maps. These actual water bodies and narrow joins account for much of the selected passage. The inlet from the unresolved eastern lowland turn and the exact selected branch through the intervening network are not fully established, so this component remains incomplete. No lake-name equivalence is inferred from regional basin membership.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern lagoon margin and selected Atlantic ending
correspondence.finding: The final selected part reaches the coast south of the lagoon’s southeastern margin, rather than the separate Laguna outlet beside Lagoa Santo Antônio. The municipal original shows the lagoon, adjacent settlement/road/boundary and Atlantic shoreline. It does not continuously establish a water-channel crossing from that lagoon margin to this selected sea ending. Coastal proximity and administrative linework are insufficient to close the gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southern glacial opening and northward approach to Neacola River
correspondence.finding: The western original shows the chosen opening on an unnamed glacier tongue confined by mountain ridges. Its northward terrain passage reaches the head of the braided Neacola valley. This establishes the bounded glacial-source setting and adjoining river corridor, without assigning Neacola River to the ice or claiming surface or subglacial hydraulic measurements.

correspondence.component_scope: Neacola River, intervening side-stream joins and approach to Kenibuna Lake
correspondence.finding: Repeated Neacola River labels and the continuous braided valley cover the selected northward, eastward and northeastern river corridor. The western and lake originals overlap through the middle valley and expose the selected delta approach into the southern side of Kenibuna Lake. Separate western and northern tributaries are distinguished rather than substituted for the chosen source.

correspondence.component_scope: Kenibuna Lake, Shamrock Lake and the selected transfer into the larger eastern lake
correspondence.finding: The original identifies Kenibuna Lake, a separately mapped Shamrock Lake beside the Shamrock Glacier toe, and the main lake to the east. A mapped outlet from Kenibuna follows the northern side of the intervening lake-and-moraine complex. The selected parts instead cross the intervening land and separate Shamrock Lake setting. The inspected cartography does not establish that selected through-transfer into the eastern lake. Nearby connected drainage and the presence of the lake labels do not fill this material gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern lake passage and outlet into Chakachatna River
correspondence.finding: The main eastern lake and its eastward outlet are exposed continuously on the original. The outlet continues as the labeled Chakachatna River past the northern glacier-margin drainage. The independent DNR plan identifies Chakachamna Lake and explicitly discusses the Chakachatna River between the lake exit and Straight Creek. River labels carried across the lake on the composite map are not treated as a formal lake-name record.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Chakachatna canyon and mainstem fragment join
correspondence.finding: The upper original and eastern original overlap through the Chakachatna corridor south of the Crater Glacier and Kidazqeni Glacier setting. The named braided river continues east through the canyon and across the stored mainstem-fragment boundary. The simplified selected mainstem locally lies beside the mapped channel; ordinary valley correspondence is supported without requiring exact banks. The separate selected tributary is assessed independently below.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Chakachatna, Straight Creek join and distributary setting
correspondence.finding: The eastern original shows the Chakachatna River leaving the mountain valley, receiving Straight Creek and continuing south. Noaukta Slough branches toward McArthur River to the west and Middle River separates toward the east. The selected continuation follows the remaining lower Chakachatna corridor rather than the western slough or the eastern Middle River. All intervening selected reaches and the approach to the lower McArthur confluence are covered at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower confluence, McArthur River and actual Cook Inlet terminal
correspondence.finding: The lower original exposes the Chakachatna-to-McArthur confluence, the short final McArthur reach and its broad coastal mouth. The actual selected mainstem endpoint is in that McArthur mouth at Cook Inlet. It is not the upstream FID 2694 joining point. The mouth setting is established without assigning an exact contemporary tidal bank or shoreline.

correspondence.component_scope: FID 2694 opening, short eastward connector and mainstem join
correspondence.finding: Both original views covering the whole short tributary show several separately south-draining small streams and intervening slopes below the Crater/Kidazqeni glacier setting, with Chakachatna River to their south. They do not show a continuous eastward waterway corresponding to the selected opening, both parts and its stored join. Neither a neighboring glacier label nor the receiving river name establishes this through-connection. No name is assigned to this selected tributary.
